first_impression.reaction: I expected fluffy 'magical traditions' filler. But 'It says plainly which meanings are documented and which are simply often told' is the kind of line I want to see. That's an honest way to frame folklore, so I kept going. Like I always do, I jumped to the FAQ and the cost question first.

journey.quote: It says plainly which meanings are documented and which are simply often told.
journey.reaction: Good. It tells me where the hard facts stop and the stories start, and the rest of the piece mostly sticks to that.

journey.section: Noivado and the ring on the right hand
journey.quote: The ring itself is the aliança, a word the Michaelis dictionary defines as a ring used as a symbol of engagement or of marriage.
journey.reaction: Citing a named dictionary instead of 'legend says' is something I can check myself. Same goes for the Priberam definitions further down.

journey.section: FAQ: How much does it cost to get married in Brazil?
journey.quote: There is no single figure. Cartório fees are set locally, so ask the cartório directly, and a fee applies to an Australian CNI and to notarial services.
journey.reaction: I came to this one first. No numbers, but it's honest about why there aren't any, and it doesn't make up a range. I'd take that over a fake 'from $X'. The last bit, 'your Wedded Advisor can cost them on your dates', is a light sales nudge, but I can live with it.

journey.section: Marrying legally in Brazil as an Australian
journey.quote: This section reflects official sources as at November 2026. It is general information, not legal advice, and requirements can change.
journey.reaction: It dates the info and admits its limits. That's exactly what I look for. The DFAT, Embassy and CNJ Resolution 175 references are concrete and I can check them.

journey.section: Consular help in Brasília and São Paulo
journey.quote: The Honorary Consulate in Rio de Janeiro offers limited services and is not authorised to perform notarial services.
journey.reaction: This is a real catch most people would miss. A practical warning like this earns more trust than any sales pitch.

journey.quote: As at 3 November 2026, Smartraveller advises Australians to "Exercise a high degree of caution" in Brazil overall because of the threat of violent crime, with no higher-level areas.
journey.reaction: A dated government source, quoted straight and not softened. A wedding company that doesn't play down the safety picture is one I'm more likely to believe.

journey.quote: For a wedding, most couples look at places outside those states.
journey.reaction: Says who? Everything else here has a source, but this line is just the writer's assumption. Small, but it's the sort of thing I notice.

journey.quote: For a wedding outside Brazil, this is the single detail most likely to differ from what Brazilian guests expect.
journey.reaction: 'The single detail most likely' is a strong claim with nothing behind it. The advice to get the curfew in writing is useful, though.

journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor is your single point of contact for venue, travel and suppliers, with the fee and inclusions agreed in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Better than most. It at least says the fee is agreed in writing up front. But it doesn't tell me how the fee works or whether they take a cut from suppliers. Fair enough on a traditions post, but it's still my first question.

unanswered_questions: How is the Wedded Advisor fee structured (flat, percentage, or included)?
Does Wedded Wonderland take commissions or mark-ups from venues or suppliers it recommends?
Has Wedded Wonderland actually planned weddings in Brazil, or for Brazilian-Australian families? Is there a real example with a budget?

turn_offs_found.quote: Brigadeiros are the best known, and many families judge a wedding by how generous the sweets table is.
turn_offs_found.why: An unsupported generalisation passed off as fact. It's minor, but it's the kind of claim I'd go and check.

turn_offs_found.quote: The ones that travel best are the ones that need nothing but people.
turn_offs_found.why: A bit of feel-good copywriting. It's harmless, but there's nothing in it.

would_share_with: My fiancée's family, for the legal and Smartraveller sections

cta_reaction.quote: If that sounds useful, [speak with a Wedded Advisor]
cta_reaction.why: It comes after the evidence, not before, and the 'fee agreed in writing' line helps. I still wouldn't enquire until I've seen how the fee works and whether there are supplier commissions somewhere else on the site. This post isn't the place to answer that.

top_3_changes: Either source or cut 'For a wedding, most couples look at places outside those states.' It's the only travel claim with no source behind it.
Soften 'this is the single detail most likely to differ' to something you can back up, e.g. 'one detail that often differs'.
Add a short link from the Wedded Advisor line to a page explaining the fee model and how supplier pricing works (not must-fix: business details are deferred).

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off quotes an exact sentence from the draft
Stayed in character as Daniel (sceptic): read the FAQ and cost section first, judged on evidence
No invented brand facts; fee model and commission questions put in unanswered_questions
No prices and deferred business details not treated as must-fix, per orchestrator
